explanation: French chauffer means to heat, so a chauffeur stoked the fires of steam engines. In the 1890s the name passed to the drivers of early motor cars, some of them steam-powered.

claims.text: French chauffeur first meant a stoker, a person who fires a steam engine, from chauffer, 'to heat'.
The original sense of chauffeur was not a coachman, a footman or a messenger.
In the 1890s the word passed to the drivers of early motor cars, some of which were steam-powered.
